newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker Maritime first half results hit by provision.
newsitem.headline: Aker Maritime first half results hit by provision.

text.p: Norwegian offshore supply company Aker Maritime ASA posted on Thursday a 23 percent rise in first-half revenues, but said overall earnings were lower than a year ago due to a 120 million crown provision.

The Oslo-based company said higher activity in operations and the acquisition of new companies boosted revenues in the first six months to 6.06 billion crowns compared with 4.94 billion in the same 1996 period.

But despite earnings also increasing in most parts of the group, half-year operating profits were down by more than a third at 96 million crowns, against 151 million crowns, due to the 120 million provision booked in the second quarter in relation to the Njord oil project.

Aker Maritime is in dispute with oil company Norsk Hydro ASA over the Njord oil development in the North Sea, which Aker claims has cost one billion crowns more than originally agreed. Norsk Hydro has offered 200 million crowns in settlement for extra work. The two companies remain in negotiations.
First-half profits before tax amounted to 94 million crowns, versus 133 million crowns, while earnings per share were posted at 0.83 crowns compared with 1.58 crowns.
Despite the provision the results beat market expectations and Aker Maritime's share opened seven crowns higher on the Oslo bourse at 126 crowns.

The company, which was formed in November 1996 after Aker ASA spun off its Oil and Gas Technology division and merged it with offshore supplier Maritime Group, said it expected a "sharp increase" in operating profits for 1997 compared with last year.
"Underlying earnings are good as a result of both positive market developments and improvements implemented within the group," the company said in a statement announcing the results.

It said the orderbook was generally good for the rest of 1997 as a whole but lay-offs were likely at some fabrication companies for short periods in the autumn. The order intake for 1998 was "satisfactory".

"This year the greatest increase in revenues and profits is expected in the group's UK and U.S. activities as a result of both new contracts and acquisitions, and in Norway, in the areas of products and operations, maintenance and modifications," the company said.
